solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: New Age greeting?

parts.note: surface reading: a salutation from the hippie, crystals-and-incense New Age movement; setter's reading: the new age you reach each year, so the greeting is the one sent on that anniversary

explanation.surface: A greeting such as a hippie spiritualist might offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Age' is read literally: on this day each year you turn a new age, and friends post you a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The greeting sent on someone's annual anniversary of being born marks the age they have just reached.

clue.text: With this pass, one may take flight

definitions.text: With this pass, one may take flight

parts.words: With this pass, one may take flight
parts.note: surface reading: a pass that lets someone escape or run away; setter's reading: to board an aeroplane, for which the airline issues a pass at check-in

explanation.surface: Someone is handed a permit that lets them flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take flight' suggests fleeing; here it means literally catching a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The document issued at check-in authorises a passenger to get on the aeroplane.

clue.text: A puzzle for the Inspector

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a picture puzzle where images stand for words or syllables
second meaning: Inspector John ..., the Edinburgh detective in Ian Rankin's novels

explanation.surface: A mystery set for a police detective to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: Rebus is the detective hero of Ian Rankin's crime novels set in Edinburgh, later televised.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a picture-word riddle and the surname of a famous fictional police inspector.

clue.text: The lion is restless: call this urgently

indicators.note: something restless will not keep still, so these letters move into a new order

parts.note: the words taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A zookeeper reports an agitated big cat and says to ring at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the answer by its use: it is the number you ring in an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotline is a direct telephone line set up for urgent or emergency calls.

clue.text: Transfer a small notice

parts.note: taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a sign is a posted notice

explanation.surface: Someone moves a little advertisement from one place to another.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign property or rights is to transfer them legally to another person.

clue.text: Examine an American method of payment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to inspect or verify
second meaning: the US spelling of a bank cheque

explanation.walkthrough: British English spells the bank instrument 'cheque'; the American spelling matches the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for inspecting something and the US spelling of a written order to a bank to pay.

clue.text: Income concerning chosen location

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning
a venue is the place picked for an event

explanation.surface: A note about earnings relating to some selected site.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is the money a business or government takes in, a synonym for earnings.

clue.text: Almost grand and mature, very well-behaved

parts.note: 'as good as' means practically or almost
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
mature in years

explanation.surface: A description of someone nearly great and grown-up, and impeccably behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: A three-word phrase is clued by a single word: 'as good as done' means almost done.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a child behaving perfectly, an expression of excellent conduct.

clue.text: A minute part in range

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for minute
a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: A tiny portion lies within some range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like the adjective meaning tiny, but it is the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit means scope or extent, the sphere within which something operates.

clue.text: Son hauls up bundles of crops

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
to heave is to lift or haul with effort

explanation.surface: A farmer's boy lifts the harvested bundles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheaves are bound bundles of cut cereal stalks left in the field at harvest.

clue.text: Dug tins out for cleaning

indicators.note: out suggests something wrong or put out of place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the words taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Someone digs old tins out of a cupboard in order to clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusting is the household chore of wiping away dust, a form of cleaning.

clue.text: Oriental fighting to finish in knockout

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, which wraps round it

parts.note: KO is the abbreviation for a knockout in boxing
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A martial art bout settled by a knockout blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords, an Eastern combat sport.

clue.text: Granny arranged to return in French city

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: set means arranged or put in place

explanation.surface: Grandmother plans a trip back to France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' looks like an anagram signal, but here it is a plain synonym for set.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a large city in western France on the Loire.

clue.text: Chart-topper, a little offensive

parts.note: the number one in the charts, written No 1 with the digit as the letter I
some means a small amount

explanation.surface: A hit record that is slightly rude.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 in 'No 1' stands in for the letter I, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means foul-smelling or very unpleasant, nothing to do with noise.

clue.text: Be flexible about home for unsold wine

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to bend is to flex
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Advice to be accommodating about where unsold wine is stored.
explanation.walkthrough: A bin end is a British term for the last bottles of a wine, sold off cheaply by a merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bin ends are leftover bottles of a line a merchant is clearing, typically discounted stock.

clue.text: Troublemaker gets to work creating strong effects

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil
acts means takes action or functions

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker sets about something and causes big consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Impacts are marked influences or consequences, powerful results of an action.

clue.text: Endlessly insolent boy is individual

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: pert means cheeky or impudent
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A permanently cheeky lad is quite a character.
explanation.definitionFit: A person is a single human being, so the noun individual is a synonym.

clue.text: Slightly damages computer parts

definitions.meaning: first meaning: knocks small pieces off an edge, as with a cup
second meaning: silicon integrated circuits inside a computer

explanation.surface: Someone does minor harm to the hardware of a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for nicking small fragments off and a noun for microprocessors.

clue.text: Having great inclination to soak

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sharply sloping, as a hill
second meaning: to leave something immersed in liquid, as tea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' suggests a keen desire, but it means a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for a sharp gradient and a verb for leaving something to soak in liquid.

clue.text: Put into words with great speed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to state or articulate
second meaning: fast, as in sending a parcel by the quickest service

explanation.surface: Someone talks very quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for articulating thoughts and also an adverb for sending by a fast service.

clue.text: The best chocolate finally with fewer calories

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the word chocolate ends in this letter
lite is the marketing spelling of light, meaning low in calories

explanation.surface: Top-quality chocolate that is also less fattening.
explanation.definitionFit: An elite is a select group regarded as superior, the cream of the crop.

clue.text: Employ these people and you might get slated

definitions.text: Employ these people and you might get slated

parts.note: surface reading: hiring them could earn you harsh criticism; setter's reading: having your house covered with slate tiles by the tradesmen you hired

explanation.surface: A warning that hiring certain people could get you panned.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage to slate is to criticise severely, but literally it means to lay slates on a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: These tradesmen lay tiles or slates on buildings, so hiring them gets a house slated.

clue.text: Put nothing on bottom of face cloth

indicators.note: in an across answer, putting one thing on another places it after, so the piece named first comes second

parts.note: the chin is the lowest part of the face
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Applying no make-up to the lower face, then a cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put nothing on' tacks the zero letter after the chin piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a twilled cotton fabric, used for the trousers named after it.

clue.text: Stay calm, unlike Anne Boleyn

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for remaining composed in a crisis
second meaning, taken literally: Henry VIII's second wife was beheaded in 1536

explanation.surface: Advice to stay composed, set beside a queen who famously did not.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half takes the idiom literally: Anne Boleyn lost her head on the block.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means remain composed under pressure; literally it means not losing one's head.
